To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GM-CSF is a potent macrophage stimulator and that GM-CSF-stimulation of macrophages can lead to disease in mice.
the disease pattern of GM-CSF transgenesis is determined by the site of transgene insertion and is likely to reflect differences in the activity of macrophages.
GM-CSF transgene insertion sites in the genome can influence disease development and the macrophage phenotype in GM-CSF-transgenic mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of a GM-CSF transgene and the resulting elevated levels of GM-CSF on the development of a spectrum of diseases in transgenic mice, and the differences in these effects in two lines of GM-CSF transgenics in which the transgene was inserted into different chromosomal sites.

the development of a model for the study of chronic inflammatory diseases in which the transgene is expressed in a tissue-specific manner, and in which the transgenic mice exhibit a spectrum of diseases that can be related to the transgene expression and the tissue distribution of the macrophage populations in the transgenic mice.
the effects of a cytokine, granulocyte-macro- phage colony-stimulat- ing factor, on the immune system and the pathogenesis of diseases in transgenic mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the disease in GM-CSF-transgenic mice is caused by the GM-CSF and is a macrophage-mediated disease.
GM-CSF transgene insertion site has a significant influence on the disease phenotype in GM-CSF overexpressing transgenic mice.
GM-CSF transgenes are capable of inducing a variety of diseases in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GM-CSF transgenics are a good model system for studying the pathophysiology of macrophage-mediated diseases.

GM-CSF transgene insertion into the X chromosome of female-line transgenic mice is a more effective means of generating a model of chronic inflammatory disease than autosomal insertion into the male-line mice.

the GM-CSF transgene induces a variety of diseases in transgenic mice, which are associated with different levels of serum GM-CS- F, different patterns of GM-CSF expression, and possibly different patterns of GM- CSF-stimulated macrophage activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the disease pattern of GM-CSF transgenics is influenced by the chromosomal location of the transgene.
the location of a transgene in the genome is a major determinant of disease phenotype in transgenic mice, and this should be taken into account in the design of transgenic experiments.
the disease phenotypes of transgenic animals are highly dependent upon the site of transgene insertion.
